subject.title: [Bug]: OpenAI-compatible streaming tool calls are dropped when provider omits finish_reason

question: Should OpenClaw execute native OpenAI-compatible streamed tool calls when `delta.tool_calls` were parsed and the raw SSE stream ended with `[DONE]`, even if no final `finish_reason` chunk was emitted?
rationale: This changes the shipped fail-closed contract at the provider-output-to-tool-execution boundary, and automation cannot choose that security/compatibility policy for maintainers.

options.title: Accept clean-DONE tool execution
options.body: Land the linked PR after normal checks, treating parsed native tool calls plus raw SSE `[DONE]` as sufficient execution intent without a final finish reason.

options.title: Require exact-provider proof first
options.body: Ask for a redacted Evolink or equivalent provider run before merge if maintainers want live proof from the originally reported route.

options.title: Keep explicit finish reasons required
options.body: Leave current fail-closed behavior in place and close or pause the linked PR if maintainers decide no-finish streamed tool calls must never execute.

recommendation.title: Accept clean-DONE tool execution
recommendation.body: Land the linked PR after normal checks, treating parsed native tool calls plus raw SSE `[DONE]` as sufficient execution intent without a final finish reason.

likelyOwner.reason: He merged the adjacent safety-contract PRs and is the clearest history-backed owner for accepting or rejecting this execution-boundary change.
